docs.title: Adding a New Blog Post
docs.text: Blog posts are stored as static data in a single TypeScript file. No CMS, database, or backend changes are needed to publish a new article. Adding a post is a four-step process.

docs.title: Where the Data Lives
docs.text:
All blog posts are defined in:

frontend/src/data/blogPosts.ts

This file exports:

  • A BlogPost TypeScript interface
  • A blogPosts array containing every post in the blog
  • A getBlogPost(slug) helper used by the individual post page

docs.title: The BlogPost Interface
docs.text:
Each entry in the array must conform to this shape:

export interface BlogPost {
  slug: string;        // URL-safe identifier, becomes the page URL
  title: string;       // Displayed as the article heading
  date: string;        // ISO 8601 format: "YYYY-MM-DD"
  description: string; // One-sentence summary shown on index and post pages
  readingTime: string; // Shown as a badge, e.g. "5 min read"
  content: string;     // Full article body as an HTML string
}

docs.title: 1. Choose a slug
docs.text:
The slug becomes the URL path: /blog/<slug>. Rules:

  • Use only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens
  • Make it descriptive and keyword-rich for SEO
  • It must be unique — no two posts can share the same slug

Example: how-to-automate-accounts-payable

docs.title: 2. Write the post content
docs.text:
The content field is an HTML string. Use standard semantic tags:

<h2>Section Heading</h2>
<p>Paragraph text.</p>
<ul>
  <li>List item</li>
</ul>
<ol>
  <li>Numbered item</li>
</ol>
<strong>Bold text</strong>
<em>Italic text</em>
<code>inline code</code>

Do not include an outer <article> or <html> wrapper — just the inner body content.

docs.title: 3. Add the entry to the array
docs.text:
Open frontend/src/data/blogPosts.ts and append a new object to the blogPosts array:

{
  slug: 'your-new-slug',
  title: 'Your Article Title',
  date: '2026-03-15',
  description: 'A one-sentence summary of the article for SEO and listing pages.',
  readingTime: '5 min read',
  content: `
    <h2>First Section</h2>
    <p>Your content here...</p>
  `,
},

Posts are displayed on the blog index in the order they appear in the array. Place the newest post at the end or reorder as needed.

docs.title: 4. Save and verify
docs.text:
Save the file. The new post is immediately available at:

  • Blog index: /blog — your post appears as a new card
  • Post page: /blog/<your-slug> — the full article is rendered

No changes to router.tsx, Navbar.tsx, or any other file are required.

docs.title: Tips for SEO-Effective Posts
docs.text:
• Title: Include the primary keyword near the start. Keep it under 60 characters so it is not truncated in search results.
  • Description: Write a compelling sentence (120–155 characters) that includes the primary keyword and a clear benefit. This becomes the meta description.
  • Content length: Aim for 600–1200 words. Cover the topic thoroughly with concrete examples and numbered steps where applicable.
  • Headings: Use <h2> for major sections and <h3> for sub-sections within them. Include keywords naturally in headings.
  • Slug: Match the slug to the article's primary keyword phrase, e.g. ocr-for-healthcare-forms rather than blog-post-12.

docs.text: File Purpose frontend/src/data/blogPosts.ts All post data — the only file you edit to add a post frontend/src/pages/BlogPage.tsx Blog index page — renders cards for every post in the array frontend/src/pages/BlogPostPage.tsx Individual post page — looks up the post by slug and renders the HTML content frontend/src/router.tsx Defines /blog and /blog/$slug routes — no changes needed for new posts frontend/src/components/Navbar.tsx Contains the BLOG navbar link — no changes needed for new posts

docs.title: Nolain OCR Backend API Usage
docs.text: This guide provides detailed information on how to interact with the Nolain OCR Backend API.

docs.title: Base URLs
docs.text:
Environment Base URL Local Terminal (uvicorn on :8000) http://localhost:8000 Local Docker (nginx) http://localhost/api VPS / Production https://nolainocr.com/api

When using Docker or production, all API routes are prefixed with /api (nginx strips the prefix before forwarding to the backend). Exceptions: /webhook and /health are routed directly without the /api prefix.

Do not call http://localhost/topup-packs without the /api prefix when using Docker; that hits the frontend, not the backend.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Most endpoints require authentication via request headers:

Header Description X-Access-Token Supabase JWT access token (preferred) X-User-Id User UUID (fallback if token unavailable)

Obtain the access token from the POST /login or POST /auth/session response.

Example:

curl -X GET "{{BASE_URL}}/subscription-status" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id"

docs.title: Health Check
docs.text:
curl "{{BASE_URL}}/"

Returns {"message": "Nolain OCR API is running"}.

docs.title: 1. User Registration
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/register" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "password": "your_password",
    "full_name": "John Doe"
  }'
Field Required Description email Yes User email address password Yes User password full_name No User's full name

docs.title: 2. User Login
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "password": "your_password"
  }'

Returns user ID, access token, and email confirmation status.

docs.title: 3. Google OAuth
docs.text:
Get redirect URL:

curl "{{BASE_URL}}/auth/google?redirect_to=https://nolainocr.com/auth/callback"

Verify session after OAuth callback:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/auth/session" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "access_token": "token_from_oauth",
    "refresh_token": "refresh_token_from_oauth"
  }'

docs.title: 4. User Logout
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/logout" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id"

Cleans up all uploaded files for the user and clears the session.

docs.title: 5. Password Reset
docs.text:
Request reset email:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/reset-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email": "user@example.com"}'

Update password with tokens from email:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/update-password" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "password": "new_password",
    "access_token": "token_from_reset_email",
    "refresh_token": "refresh_token_from_reset_email"
  }'

docs.title: 6. Upload PDF Files
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/upload_pdf" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id" \
  -F "files=@/path/to/document.pdf"

Multiple files:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/upload_pdf" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id" \
  -F "files=@/path/to/doc1.pdf" \
  -F "files=@/path/to/doc2.pdf"
Field Required Description files Yes One or more PDF files (multipart/form-data)

Response: - Single page: file_id is the filename (e.g., "image.jpg") - Multiple pages: file_id is a folder name (e.g., "upload_userid_timestamp") - PDFs are converted to page_N.jpg images automatically

Page limits (enforced at upload):

Tier Pages/Document Pages/Month Free 3 3 Pro 50 1,500 Pro Plus 200 10,000

docs.title: 7. Upload Image Files
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/upload_image" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id" \
  -F "files=@/path/to/image.jpg"

Same behavior as PDF upload but for image files directly (.png, .jpg, .jpeg).

docs.title: 8. Extract Text from Single Image
docs.text:
Synchronous extraction — returns results immediately.

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/extract_image" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id" \
  -d '{
    "file_id": "your_file_id_from_upload",
    "extraction_mode": "fast_extraction",
    "user_id": "your_user_id"
  }'
Field Required Description file_id Yes Filename or folder path from upload extraction_mode Yes "fast_extraction" (only mode available) user_id Yes User ID (must match authenticated user)

docs.title: 9. Extract Multiple Images (Async)
docs.text:
Queues a Celery task and returns a task_id. Connect to the SSE stream for progress and results.

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/extract_multiple_images" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id" \
  -d '{
    "folder_id": "upload_userid_timestamp",
    "extraction_mode": "fast_extraction",
    "user_id": "your_user_id"
  }'

With template groups (combine pages into multi-page documents):

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/extract_multiple_images" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id" \
  -d '{
    "folder_id": "upload_userid_timestamp",
    "extraction_mode": "fast_extraction",
    "user_id": "your_user_id",
    "template_group": [
      ["page_1.jpg", "page_2.jpg"],
      ["page_3.jpg"]
    ]
  }'
Field Required Description folder_id Yes Folder from multi-page upload (must start with upload_) extraction_mode Yes "fast_extraction" user_id Yes User ID template_group No List of page groups (1–4 images per group)

Response: Returns task_id. Listen for results:

curl -N "{{BASE_URL}}/stream/{task_id}"

SSE events contain status (processing, completed, failed), progress (0–100), and results on completion.

docs.title: 10. Get Page Image
docs.text:
Preview a specific page from an uploaded folder:

curl "{{BASE_URL}}/get_page_image/upload_userid_timestamp/0" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token"
Parameter Description folder_id Folder name from upload page_number Zero-based page index (0, 1, 2, ...)

Returns JPEG image with cache headers.

docs.title: 11. Export Current Data
docs.text:
Export the current extraction table as Excel or CSV:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/export_current_data" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -d '{
    "data": {
      "patient_name": ["John", "Jane"],
      "diagnosis": ["Flu", "Cold"]
    },
    "format": "excel",
    "filename": "my_export",
    "columns": ["patient_name", "diagnosis"]
  }'
Field Required Description data Yes Columnar extraction data format No "excel" or "csv" (default: "excel") filename No Export filename (default: "extraction") columns No Subset of columns to include

Returns file download. JSON export is handled client-side.

docs.title: 12. Get Subscription Status
docs.text:
curl "{{BASE_URL}}/subscription-status" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id"

Returns plan tier, usage, limits, top-up credit balance, and Stripe subscription details.

docs.title: 13. Get Subscription Limits
docs.text:
curl "{{BASE_URL}}/subscription-limits"

No auth required. Returns limits and pricing for all tiers.

docs.title: 14. Create Checkout Session (Subscription)
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/create-checkout-session" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "your_user_id",
    "price_id": "price_xxx"
  }'

Returns Stripe Checkout URL for subscription purchase.

docs.title: 15. Update Subscription
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/update-subscription" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "your_user_id",
    "new_price_id": "price_xxx"
  }'

Upgrades (Pro → Pro+) take effect immediately. Downgrades are scheduled at period end.

docs.title: 16. Cancel Subscription
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/cancel-subscription" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id"

Schedules cancellation at the end of the current billing period.

docs.title: 17. Create Billing Portal Session
docs.text:
curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/create-billing-portal-session" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -H "X-User-Id: your_user_id"

Returns URL to Stripe Customer Portal for payment method and subscription management.

docs.title: 18. Top-up Page Packs
docs.text:
List available packs:

curl "{{BASE_URL}}/topup-packs"

Create top-up checkout:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/create-topup-checkout" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "your_user_id",
    "pack_id": "topup_5"
  }'

Confirm top-up after payment:

curl -X POST "{{BASE_URL}}/confirm-topup-checkout" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Access-Token: your_jwt_token" \
  -d '{
    "session_id": "cs_test_xxx"
  }'

Top-up credits are consumed after monthly plan quota is exhausted. Free-tier users can also purchase top-ups.

docs.title: 19. Stripe Webhook
docs.text:
Called by Stripe, not by your application:

POST /webhook

In local development:

stripe listen --forward-to localhost/webhook

docs.title: 20. SSE Task Stream
docs.text:
Real-time extraction progress:

curl -N "{{BASE_URL}}/stream/{task_id}"

No auth required. Events are JSON with status, progress, and results fields.

docs.title: Page Billing
docs.text:
Pages are billed after extraction completes:

  1. Monthly plan quota is consumed first
  2. Top-up credits are used when monthly quota is exhausted
  3. Returns 402 Payment Required if both pools are empty

Admin users (ADMIN_USER_ID env var) bypass all limits.

docs.text:
The following endpoints existed in earlier versions but are no longer available:

Endpoint Status GET /historical_names/{user_id} Removed GET /export_historical/{user_id}/{name} Removed — use POST /export_current_data POST /numerical-statistics Removed POST /categorical-*-statistics Removed POST /pearson-correlations Removed GET /task-updates/{task_id} Renamed to GET /stream/{task_id} GET /subscription-status/{user_id} Now GET /subscription-status (auth header) POST /cancel-subscription/{user_id} Now POST /cancel-subscription (auth header)

Extraction modes new_historical and update_historical are no longer supported. Only fast_extraction is available.

docs.title: Reuse Auth and Stripe
docs.text:
This guide is split into focused instruction files:

  1. Project structure and files to copy
  2. Configure Supabase and Google
  3. Configure Stripe
  4. Optional one-time credits
  5. Test the integration

Use a new Supabase project and Stripe account/project for the new app. Do not copy API keys, webhook secrets, customer IDs, product IDs, or Price IDs from this project.

docs.title: Current: Celery + Redis
docs.text: Pros: Mature (10+ years), Python-native, retry logic, flexible routing Cons: Separate worker process, Redis dependency

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
1. BullMQ: Modern, but Node.js (backend is Python)
  2. AWS SQS + Lambda: Fully managed, but vendor lock-in, cold starts
  3. RabbitMQ + Celery: More robust broker, but overkill for our scale
  4. Dramatiq: Simpler than Celery, but smaller ecosystem
  5. FastAPI Background Tasks: Built-in, but no persistence or retries

docs.title: Why Celery + Redis
docs.text:
• Mature and stable
  • Python-native (fits our stack)
  • Retry logic built-in
  • Redis sufficient for our scale
  • Good documentation

docs.title: When to Reconsider
docs.text:
• AWS SQS if moving to cloud and need massive scale
  • Dramatiq if starting fresh and want simpler API

docs.title: Current: Mistral AI Vision
docs.text: Pros: High accuracy, structured JSON, batch API, multi-language Cons: API cost ($0.001-0.003/page), rate limits, vendor lock-in

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
1. Tesseract (Open Source): Free, local, but lower accuracy, no structured output
  2. AWS Textract: Similar cost/accuracy, AWS lock-in, no batch discount
  3. Google Vision: Similar cost, no structured extraction
  4. GPT-4 Vision: 2-5x more expensive, similar capabilities
  5. Azure Form Recognizer: Higher complexity, more expensive

docs.title: Why Mistral AI
docs.text:
• Best balance of cost, accuracy, and structured output
  • Batch API for scale
  • Good documentation

docs.title: Current: Zustand
docs.text: Pros: Minimal boilerplate, TypeScript support, persist middleware, small (1KB) Cons: Less ecosystem than Redux, no built-in dev tools

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
1. Redux Toolkit: Large ecosystem, dev tools, but more boilerplate
  2. Jotai: Atomic state, minimal, but different mental model
  3. Recoil: Facebook's solution, but experimental
  4. Context API: No dependency, but performance issues

docs.title: Why Zustand
docs.text:
• Simplicity (minimal API)
  • Small bundle size
  • Built-in persistence
  • Fast development

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
1. Self-hosted PostgreSQL: Full control, but requires management
  2. MongoDB Atlas: NoSQL flexibility, but need separate auth
  3. Firebase: All-in-one, but NoSQL limitations
  4. AWS RDS + Cognito: Enterprise-grade, but complex and costly

docs.title: Why Supabase
docs.text:
• Speed of development (Auth + DB integrated)
  • PostgreSQL power (JSONB support)
  • Cost-effective free tier
  • Managed service (no DB admin)

docs.title: Migration Path
docs.text: Can migrate to self-hosted PostgreSQL if needed (2-4 weeks effort)

docs.title: Endpoint Modules
docs.text:
health.py - GET / - Health check

auth.py - Authentication & User Management - POST /login - Email/password login - POST /register - User registration - GET /auth/google - Google OAuth redirect URL - POST /auth/session - Verify OAuth tokens after callback - POST /logout - Logout and file cleanup (auth required) - POST /reset-password - Request password reset - POST /update-password - Update password with recovery tokens

documents.py - Document Processing - POST /upload_pdf - Upload PDF(s), convert to page images - POST /upload_image - Upload image file(s) - GET /get_page_image/{folder_id}/{page_number} - Preview pages - POST /extract_image - Synchronous single-image extraction - POST /extract_multiple_images - Async batch extraction (returns task_id) - POST /export_current_data - Export current table data as Excel or CSV

payments.py - Subscription Management - POST /create-checkout-session - Start Stripe subscription checkout - POST /webhook - Stripe webhook handler - GET /subscription-limits - Plan limits for all tiers - GET /subscription-status - Current plan, usage, top-up balance (auth required) - POST /cancel-subscription - Cancel at period end (auth required) - POST /create-billing-portal-session - Stripe Customer Portal (auth required) - POST /update-subscription - Upgrade/downgrade plan (auth required)

topup_billing.py - One-time Page Packs - GET /topup-packs - Catalog of available top-up packs - POST /create-topup-checkout - Start Stripe checkout for page credits - POST /confirm-topup-checkout - Confirm paid session and credit pages

sse.py - Real-time Updates - GET /stream/{task_id} - SSE stream for Celery extraction progress

docs.title: Auth Dependencies (dependencies/auth.py)
docs.text:
Protected endpoints require one of: - X-Access-Token header (Supabase JWT — preferred) - X-User-Id header (fallback)

Returns AuthContext with user and method: "session".

docs.title: 2. Service Layer (services/)
docs.text: Business logic layer. Separates API concerns from implementation.

docs.title: auth_service.py
docs.text:
• User registration and login via Supabase Auth
  • Google OAuth URL generation and session verification
  • Password reset and update flows
  • Logout with upload file cleanup

docs.title: upload_service.py
docs.text:
• PDF and image upload handling
  • PDF to JPEG conversion (pdf2image/Poppler)
  • Page limit validation before upload
  • Page image serving for preview
  • Tracks file paths in user_sessions table

docs.title: extraction_service.py
docs.text:
• Single image: synchronous Mistral vision extraction in the API process
  • Multiple images: queues Celery task, returns task_id immediately
  • Template grouping (combine up to 4 pages per document)
  • Schema extraction from first page, then batch processing of remaining pages

docs.title: export_service.py
docs.text:
• Excel and CSV export from current extraction table data
  • Background task cleanup of temporary export files

docs.title: payment_service.py
docs.text:
• Stripe checkout session creation (subscriptions and top-ups)
  • Subscription status, cancellation, plan changes
  • Billing portal access
  • Webhook event processing

Webhook Events Handled: - checkout.session.completed - Create subscription or credit top-up pages - customer.subscription.updated - Update subscription - customer.subscription.deleted - Cancel subscription - invoice.payment_succeeded - Reset monthly usage counter

docs.title: page_billing_service.py
docs.text:
• Bills processed pages after extraction completes
  • Priority: monthly plan quota first, then top-up credits
  • Returns 402 if both pools exhausted
  • Admin users (ADMIN_USER_ID) bypass limits

docs.title: billing_service.py
docs.text: • Billing mode helpers (subscription + top-up can coexist)

docs.title: extraction_pipeline.py
docs.text:
• Mistral AI vision API calls (single and batch)
  • Parallel async extraction for <50 images
  • Mistral Batch API for ≥50 images
  • JSON parsing and schema enforcement

docs.title: key_standardization.py
docs.text:
• Flatten nested dictionaries
  • Key normalization (lowercase, underscores)
  • extract_schema() from first extraction result
  • Sentence transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) for key similarity matching

docs.title: type_conversion.py
docs.text: • String to number/date coercion for export

docs.title: file_utils.py / image_utils.py
docs.text:
• PDF page counting and conversion
  • Base64 image encoding
  • Multi-page image combining (template groups)

docs.title: storage.py
docs.text:
• Excel generation (openpyxl)
  • CSV generation

docs.title: supabase_client.py
docs.text:
• All database operations (subscriptions, user_sessions, topup_credit_purchases)
  • Three client modes: default (service role preferred), auth-only (anon key), billing client

docs.title: 4. Background Tasks (tasks/extraction.py)
docs.text:
Celery Task: process_extraction_task

Flow: 1. Publish "processing" status to Redis 2. Load and group images (template_group support) 3. Extract schema from first page 4. Process remaining pages (parallel or batch API) 5. Convert results to columnar format 6. Bill processed pages via page_billing_service 7. Publish "completed" or "failed" status with results

docs.title: config.py
docs.text:
Key settings: Supabase credentials, Mistral API key, Stripe keys/price IDs, subscription limits, Celery/Redis URLs, FRONTEND_URL, ADMIN_USER_ID.

Subscription Limits (backend defaults):

FREE_PAGES_PER_DOCUMENT = 3
FREE_PAGES_PER_MONTH = 3
PRO_PAGES_PER_DOCUMENT = 50
PRO_PAGES_PER_MONTH = 1500
PRO_PLUS_PAGES_PER_DOCUMENT = 200
PRO_PLUS_PAGES_PER_MONTH = 10000

docs.title: celery_app.py
docs.text:
• Broker and result backend: Redis
  • Task discovery: backend.tasks
  • Serializer: JSON

docs.title: redis_client.py
docs.text: • Pub/Sub channels: task_updates:{task_id}

docs.title: clients.py
docs.text: • Singleton Mistral AI client

docs.title: 6. Layout Module (layout/) — Experimental
docs.text: YOLO-based document layout detection. Not wired into the production extraction pipeline.

docs.title: Example 1: Single Image Extraction (Synchronous)
docs.text:
1. POST /extract_image (X-Access-Token header)
   ↓
2. ExtractionService.extract_image()
   ↓
3. extraction_pipeline: Mistral vision API call
   ↓
4. Flatten, normalize keys, convert types
   ↓
5. bill_processed_pages()
   ↓
6. Return extracted data

docs.title: Example 2: Multi-Image Extraction (Async)
docs.text:
1. POST /extract_multiple_images
   ↓
2. ExtractionService.extract_multiple_images()
   ↓
3. Queue Celery task → process_extraction_task()
   ↓
4. Return task_id immediately

[Frontend connects to GET /stream/{task_id}]

[Celery Worker]
5. Extract schema from page 1
6. Batch process remaining pages
7. Bill pages, publish results to Redis
8. Frontend receives via SSE

docs.title: Key Design Patterns
docs.text:
1. Service Layer Pattern: Separates API from business logic
  2. Singleton Pattern: Shared Mistral AI client
  3. Repository Pattern: supabase_client.py abstracts database
  4. Pub/Sub Pattern: Redis for real-time progress updates
  5. Task Queue Pattern: Celery for long-running operations
  6. Dual Billing Pool: Plan quota + top-up credits with priority ordering

docs.title: Data Flow Architecture
docs.text: This document details the end-to-end data flows through the Nolain OCR system for key user workflows.

docs.title: Flow 1: User Registration and Email Verification
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Supabase
    participant Email

    User->>Frontend: Fill registration form
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /register
    Backend->>Supabase: Create user account
    Supabase-->>Backend: User created
    Backend->>Supabase: Create free subscription record
    Supabase->>Email: Send verification email
    Backend-->>Frontend: Registration success
    Frontend-->>User: Show "Check your email"

    User->>Email: Click verification link
    Email->>Frontend: Redirect to / with tokens
    Frontend->>Frontend: Detect verification tokens
    Frontend->>Frontend: Redirect to /registration-success
    Frontend-->>User: "Email verified! Sign in"

docs.title: Flow 2: User Login (Email/Password)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Supabase

    User->>Frontend: Enter email/password
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /login
    Backend->>Supabase: Authenticate user
    Supabase-->>Backend: User data + access_token
    Backend-->>Frontend: User data + access_token
    Frontend->>Frontend: Store in authStore
    Frontend->>Frontend: Redirect to /dashboard
    Frontend-->>User: Dashboard page

Subsequent API calls include headers: - X-Access-Token: {access_token} - X-User-Id: {user_id}

docs.title: Flow 2b: Google OAuth Login
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Supabase
    participant Backend

    User->>Frontend: Click "Sign in with Google"
    Frontend->>Supabase: signInWithOAuth (Google)
    Supabase-->>User: Google consent screen
    User->>Supabase: Authorize
    Supabase->>Frontend: Redirect to /auth/callback?code=...
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /auth/session (tokens)
    Backend->>Supabase: Verify tokens
    Backend-->>Frontend: User data
    Frontend->>Frontend: Store in authStore
    Frontend-->>User: Redirect to /dashboard

docs.title: Flow 3: Document Upload (Single Page)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Supabase
    participant Filesystem

    User->>Frontend: Select PDF/image file
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /upload_pdf (X-Access-Token)
    Backend->>Supabase: Check subscription limits
    Backend->>Backend: Validate page count
    Backend->>Filesystem: Save file to data/
    Backend->>Supabase: Update user_sessions (file_paths)
    Backend-->>Frontend: file_id (filename)
    Frontend->>Frontend: Store in dashboardStore
    Frontend-->>User: Show preview + extract options

docs.title: Flow 4: Document Upload (Multi-Page)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Supabase
    participant Filesystem

    User->>Frontend: Select multiple files or multi-page PDF
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /upload_pdf (multiple files)
    Backend->>Supabase: Check subscription limits
    Backend->>Backend: Validate total page count
    Backend->>Filesystem: Create folder upload_{user_id}_{timestamp}/
    Backend->>Filesystem: Convert PDF pages to page_N.jpg
    Backend->>Supabase: Update user_sessions (file_paths)
    Backend-->>Frontend: file_id (folder name)
    Frontend->>Backend: GET /get_page_image/{folder_id}/{n}
    Backend-->>Frontend: Page image URLs
    Frontend-->>User: Show page grid + template config

Folder Structure:

backend/data/
└── upload_{user_id}_{timestamp}/
    ├── page_1.jpg
    ├── page_2.jpg
    └── ...

docs.title: Flow 5: Single Image Extraction (Synchronous)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant MistralAI
    participant Supabase

    User->>Frontend: Click "Extract"
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /extract_image
    Backend->>Backend: Load and encode image
    Backend->>MistralAI: Vision API call
    MistralAI-->>Backend: JSON structured data
    Backend->>Backend: Flatten, normalize keys, convert types
    Backend->>Supabase: bill_processed_pages()
    Backend-->>Frontend: Extracted data
    Frontend->>Frontend: Store in dashboardStore
    Frontend-->>User: Display in DataTable

docs.title: Flow 6: Multi-Image Extraction (Async with SSE)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Redis
    participant Celery
    participant MistralAI
    participant Supabase

    User->>Frontend: Click "Extract All"
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /extract_multiple_images
    Backend->>Redis: Queue Celery task
    Backend-->>Frontend: task_id
    Frontend->>Backend: GET /stream/{task_id} (SSE)
    Backend->>Redis: Subscribe to task_updates:{task_id}

    Celery->>Redis: Pick up task
    Celery->>Redis: Publish "processing"
    Redis-->>Backend: Status update
    Backend-->>Frontend: SSE: processing
    Frontend-->>User: Show progress bar

    Celery->>MistralAI: Extract schema from page 1
    Celery->>MistralAI: Batch/parallel process remaining pages
    Celery->>Redis: Publish progress %
    Redis-->>Backend: Progress update
    Backend-->>Frontend: SSE: progress

    Celery->>Supabase: bill_processed_pages()
    Celery->>Redis: Publish "completed" with results
    Redis-->>Backend: Final status
    Backend-->>Frontend: SSE: completed + data
    Frontend-->>User: Display results

docs.title: Flow 7: Export Current Data
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend

    User->>Frontend: Click "Export" (Excel/CSV/JSON)

    alt JSON export
        Frontend->>Frontend: Client-side download
    else Excel or CSV
        Frontend->>Backend: POST /export_current_data
        Backend->>Backend: Generate file (openpyxl or CSV)
        Backend-->>Frontend: File download
    end

    Frontend-->>User: Browser downloads file

Google Sheets export is handled entirely client-side via the Google API.

docs.title: Flow 8: Subscription Purchase
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Stripe
    participant Supabase

    User->>Frontend: Click "Upgrade to Pro"
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /create-checkout-session
    Backend->>Stripe: Create checkout session
    Stripe-->>Backend: Session URL
    Backend-->>Frontend: Redirect URL
    Frontend->>Stripe: Redirect to Stripe Checkout
    User->>Stripe: Complete purchase

    Stripe->>Backend: POST /webhook (checkout.session.completed)
    Backend->>Supabase: UPDATE subscriptions table
    Backend-->>Stripe: 200 OK

    Stripe->>Frontend: Redirect to success URL
    Frontend->>Backend: GET /subscription-status
    Backend-->>Frontend: Updated plan + limits
    Frontend-->>User: "Subscription activated!"

docs.title: Flow 9: Top-up Page Pack Purchase
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Stripe
    participant Supabase

    User->>Frontend: Select top-up pack on /account
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /create-topup-checkout
    Backend->>Stripe: Create one-time checkout session
    Stripe-->>Backend: Session URL
    Frontend->>Stripe: Redirect to checkout
    User->>Stripe: Complete payment

    Stripe->>Backend: POST /webhook (checkout.session.completed)
    Backend->>Supabase: Credit topup_page_credits

    Stripe->>Frontend: Redirect to /account?topup=success
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /confirm-topup-checkout
    Backend->>Supabase: Idempotent credit confirmation
    Frontend-->>User: Updated credit balance

docs.title: Flow 10: Password Reset
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Supabase
    participant Email

    User->>Frontend: Click "Forgot password?"
    User->>Frontend: Enter email
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /reset-password
    Backend->>Supabase: Request password reset
    Supabase->>Email: Send reset email
    Backend-->>Frontend: Success
    Frontend-->>User: "Check your email"

    User->>Email: Click reset link
    Email->>Frontend: Redirect to /reset-password?access_token=...
    User->>Frontend: Enter new password
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /update-password
    Backend->>Supabase: Update password with tokens
    Backend-->>Frontend: Success
    Frontend-->>User: "Password updated! Please log in"

docs.title: Flow 11: Logout and File Cleanup
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Supabase
    participant Filesystem

    User->>Frontend: Click logout
    Frontend->>Backend: POST /logout (X-Access-Token)
    Backend->>Supabase: Query user_sessions (file_paths)
    Backend->>Filesystem: Delete all upload folders
    Backend->>Supabase: Delete user_sessions entry
    Backend-->>Frontend: Success
    Frontend->>Frontend: Clear authStore + dashboardStore
    Frontend-->>User: Redirect to landing page

docs.title: 1. Backend Service
docs.text:
Image: nolain-ocr-backend:latest

Dockerfile:

FROM python:3.11-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y poppler-utils libgl1 libglib2.0-0
COPY requirements.txt ./
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY backend/ ./backend/
RUN mkdir -p ./backend/data

Key Features: - Python 3.11 base - Poppler-utils for PDF processing - Installs all Python dependencies - Creates data directory for uploads - Runs Uvicorn ASGI server

docs.title: Local Development (nginx-local.conf or nginx.conf)
docs.text:
upstream backend {
    server backend:8000;
}

upstream frontend {
    server frontend:80;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name localhost;
    client_max_body_size 50M;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://frontend;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-User-ID $http_x_user_id;
        proxy_set_header X-Access-Token $http_x_access_token;
    }

    location /api/ {
        rewrite ^/api/(.*)$ /$1 break;
        proxy_pass http://backend;
        proxy_set_header X-User-ID $http_x_user_id;
        proxy_set_header X-Access-Token $http_x_access_token;
    }

    # Stripe webhooks (stripe listen --forward-to http://localhost/webhook)
    location = /webhook {
        proxy_pass http://backend/webhook;
    }

    location /health {
        proxy_pass http://backend/;
    }
}

docs.title: Production (nginx-production.conf)
docs.text:
# HTTP → HTTPS redirect
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name nolainocr.com www.nolainocr.com;

    location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ {
        root /var/www/certbot;
    }

    location / {
        return 301 https://$server_name$request_uri;
    }
}

# HTTPS server
server {
    listen 443 ssl http2;
    server_name nolainocr.com www.nolainocr.com;

    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/nolainocr.com/fullchain.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/nolainocr.com/privkey.pem;

    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;

    # Security headers
    add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;
    add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
    add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;

    client_max_body_size 100M;

    # Extended timeouts for long-running API requests
    proxy_read_timeout 300s;
    proxy_connect_timeout 300s;
    proxy_send_timeout 300s;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://frontend;
        # No-cache for HTML files
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate";
    }

    location /api/ {
        rewrite ^/api/(.*)$ /$1 break;
        proxy_pass http://backend;
    }

    location = /webhook {
        proxy_pass http://backend/webhook;
    }
}

docs.title: Frontend SPA Routing (frontend/nginx.conf)
docs.text:
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name localhost;
    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    index index.html;

    # No cache for index.html
    location = /index.html {
        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate";
    }

    # Aggressive caching for static assets
    location ~* \.(js|css|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|ico|svg|woff|woff2|ttf|eot)$ {
        expires 1y;
        add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
    }

    # SPA routing: all routes → index.html
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
    }
}

docs.title: 1. Client Layer
docs.text:
• Web Browser: User interface accessed via standard web browsers
  • Supports all modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

docs.title: 2. Reverse Proxy Layer
docs.text:
• Nginx: Entry point for all HTTP/HTTPS traffic
  • Routes / to Frontend (React SPA)
  • Routes /api/* to Backend (strips /api prefix)
  • Routes /webhook directly to Backend (Stripe webhooks)
  • Routes /health to Backend health check
  • Handles SSL/TLS termination in production
  • Security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
  • Request size limits (50MB local, 100MB production)
  • Forwards auth headers (X-User-ID, X-Access-Token)

• React SPA: Single-page application built with Vite
  • TypeScript for type safety
  • Tailwind CSS for styling

docs.title: Asynchronous Task Processing
docs.text: This document explains how the system handles long-running tasks using Celery and Redis.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Asynchronous task processing allows the system to: - Handle time-consuming operations without blocking HTTP requests - Process multiple documents in parallel - Provide real-time progress updates to users - Retry failed tasks automatically

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
Celery: Distributed task queue - Picks up tasks from Redis - Executes background jobs - Reports progress and results

Redis: Message broker and result backend - Stores task queue - Stores task results (temporary) - Pub/Sub for real-time updates

FastAPI Backend: Task producer - Queues tasks via Celery - Subscribes to progress updates - Streams updates to frontend via SSE

docs.title: Task Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Frontend
    participant Backend
    participant Redis
    participant Celery

    Frontend->>Backend: POST /extract_multiple_images
    Backend->>Redis: Queue task
    Backend-->>Frontend: task_id

    Frontend->>Backend: GET /stream/{task_id} (SSE)
    Backend->>Redis: Subscribe to channel

    Celery->>Redis: Get task
    Celery->>Redis: Publish "processing"
    Redis-->>Backend: Event
    Backend-->>Frontend: SSE: processing

    loop Process images
        Celery->>Redis: Publish progress%
        Redis-->>Backend: Event
        Backend-->>Frontend: SSE: progress
    end

    Celery->>Redis: Publish "completed"
    Redis-->>Backend: Event
    Backend-->>Frontend: SSE: completed + results

docs.text:
@celery_app.task(bind=True)
def process_extraction_task(
    self,
    folder_id: str,
    user_id: str,
    template_group: list | None = None
):
    task_id = self.request.id

    # Publish initial status
    redis_client.publish(f"task_updates:{task_id}", json.dumps({
        "status": "processing",
        "progress": 0
    }))

    try:
        # Load images
        images = load_images_from_folder(folder_id)

        # Group by template if specified
        if template_group:
            image_groups = group_images(images, template_group)
        else:
            image_groups = [[img] for img in images]

        # Process each group
        results = []
        for i, group in enumerate(image_groups):
            # Extract
            if len(group) > 1:
                combined = combine_images(group)
                result = extract_text_from_image(combined, user_id)
            else:
                result = extract_text_from_image(group[0], user_id)

            results.append(result)

            # Publish progress
            progress = int((i + 1) / len(image_groups) * 100)
            redis_client.publish(f"task_updates:{task_id}", json.dumps({
                "status": "processing",
                "progress": progress
            }))

        # Bill processed pages
        bill_processed_pages(user_id, len(image_groups))

        # Publish completion
        redis_client.publish(f"task_updates:{task_id}", json.dumps({
            "status": "completed",
            "progress": 100,
            "results": results
        }))

        return {"status": "completed", "results": results}

    except Exception as e:
        # Publish failure
        redis_client.publish(f"task_updates:{task_id}", json.dumps({
            "status": "failed",
            "error": str(e)
        }))
        raise

docs.title: SSE Endpoint (api/api_v1/endpoints/sse.py)
docs.text:
@router.get("/stream/{task_id}")
async def task_updates_stream(task_id: str):
    async def event_generator():
        pubsub = redis_client.pubsub()
        pubsub.subscribe(f"task_updates:{task_id}")

        try:
            for message in pubsub.listen():
                if message['type'] == 'message':
                    data = message['data'].decode('utf-8')
                    yield f"data: {data}\n\n"

                    # Close on completion or failure
                    parsed = json.parse(data)
                    if parsed['status'] in ['completed', 'failed']:
                        break
        finally:
            pubsub.unsubscribe()
            pubsub.close()

    return EventSourceResponse(event_generator())

    updateProgressBar(data.progress)
  } else if (data.status === 'completed') {

    eventSource.close()
  } else if (data.status === 'failed') {

  }
}

Flow (single image): 1. Upload image/PDF 2. Extract text using Mistral AI vision 3. Flatten and normalize data 4. Bill processed pages 5. Return results synchronously

Flow (multiple images): 1. Upload files to folder 2. Queue Celery task → returns task_id 3. Extract schema from first page 4. Batch process remaining pages (parallel or Mistral Batch API) 5. Bill pages, publish results via SSE 6. Frontend receives results on /stream/{task_id}

}

    ["page_3.jpg", "page_4.jpg", "page_5.jpg"],

Maximum: 4 pages per combined document

docs.text:

  1. Monthly plan quota consumed first (free tier or subscription)
  2. Top-up credits consumed when monthly quota is exhausted
  3. 402 error if both pools are empty

Admin users (ADMIN_USER_ID) bypass all limits.

docs.title: Upload Process
docs.text:
Single Page:

1. Validate file type
2. Check subscription limits
3. Save to backend/data/
4. Create user_sessions entry
5. Return file_id (filename)

Multiple Pages:

1. Validate file types
2. Check total page count vs limits
3. Create folder: upload_{user_id}_{timestamp}/
4. Convert PDFs to images
5. Save all images to folder
6. Create user_sessions entry
7. Return file_id (folder name)

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
Library: pdf2image (uses Poppler)

Steps: 1. Load PDF file 2. Convert each page to PIL Image 3. Save as JPG (quality: 95%) 4. Store in folder

Example:

from pdf2image import convert_from_path

images = convert_from_path(pdf_path)
for i, image in enumerate(images):
    output_path = f"page_{i+1}.jpg"
    image.save(output_path, 'JPEG', quality=95)

Process: 1. Query user_sessions for file_paths array 2. Delete all file/folder paths from filesystem 3. Delete user_sessions entry

Example:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Nolain OCR application uses Stripe for two billing models:

  1. Recurring subscriptions — Pro ($9/mo) and Pro Plus ($29/mo) plans with monthly page quotas
  2. One-time top-up packs — Page credits ($2 / $5 / $10 / $15) that overflow monthly quota

Both can coexist: monthly plan quota is consumed first, then top-up credits.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Frontend (AccountPage, LandingPage)
    ↓
Backend (payment_service.py, page_billing_service.py)
    ↓
Stripe (Checkout, Customer Portal, Webhooks)
    ↓
Supabase (subscriptions, topup_credit_purchases tables)

docs.title: Subscription Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Checkout: User selects a plan → POST /create-checkout-session → Stripe Checkout
  2. Webhook: checkout.session.completed → backend creates/updates subscriptions record
  3. Usage: Pages billed after extraction via page_billing_service
  4. Renewal: invoice.payment_succeeded resets total_pages_processed counter
  5. Management: Users access Stripe Customer Portal via POST /create-billing-portal-session
  6. Plan changes: POST /update-subscription for upgrades (immediate) or downgrades (at period end)
  7. Cancellation: POST /cancel-subscription schedules cancellation at period end

docs.title: Top-up Pack Lifecycle
docs.text:
1. Browse: GET /topup-packs returns available packs and per-page rates
  2. Checkout: POST /create-topup-checkout → Stripe one-time payment
  3. Webhook: checkout.session.completed → credit topup_page_credits in subscriptions
  4. Confirm: POST /confirm-topup-checkout for idempotent credit confirmation
  5. Usage: Top-up credits consumed only after monthly plan quota is exhausted

docs.title: Top-up Pack Tiers
docs.text:
Pack Default Price Per-Page Rate Small $2 $0.35/page Medium $5 $0.30/page Large $10 $0.20/page XL $15 $0.15/page

Configured via STRIPE_API_TOPUP_{2,5,10,15}_PRICE_ID and API_TOPUP_* env vars. Packs without a Stripe Price ID are hidden from the catalog.

docs.title: Page Billing Priority
docs.text:
1. Monthly plan quota (free tier or active subscription)
2. Top-up page credits (overflow)
3. 402 Payment Required if both exhausted

Admin users (ADMIN_USER_ID) bypass all limits.

docs.title: subscriptions table
docs.text: Column Purpose user_id Supabase auth UUID plan_tier free, pro, pro_plus status free, active, canceled, past_due stripe_customer_id Stripe customer stripe_subscription_id Active subscription topup_page_credits Overflow page balance total_pages_processed Monthly usage counter current_period_start/end Billing period cancel_at_period_end Scheduled cancellation flag

docs.title: topup_credit_purchases table
docs.text: Idempotent record of completed top-up checkouts (stripe_session_id unique).

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Secret Keys: Never expose STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET on the frontend
  2. Webhook Verification: Backend verifies signature on every webhook event
  3. HTTPS: Required for production webhook endpoints
  4. Service Role Key: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY required for webhook writes under RLS

docs.title: Local Development
docs.text:
Forward Stripe webhooks to the local backend:

stripe listen --forward-to localhost/webhook

Copy the webhook signing secret to STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env.

For API calls through Docker nginx, use localhost/webhook (not /api/webhook).

docs.title: Webhook Issues
docs.text:
• Verify STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET matches the Stripe Dashboard (or stripe listen output)
  • Check the Events tab in Stripe Dashboard for delivery logs
  • Ensure the server is accessible from the internet (production)

docs.title: Subscription Sync Issues
docs.text:
• Check backend logs for webhook processing errors
  • Verify user_id in metadata matches the database record
  • Ensure SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is set for RLS bypass

docs.title: Top-up Credits Not Applied
docs.text:
• Check topup_credit_purchases for duplicate stripe_session_id
  • Verify STRIPE_API_TOPUP_*_PRICE_ID env vars are set
  • Call POST /confirm-topup-checkout after redirect

docs.text:

  2. Open the .env file using a text editor (e.g., nano): bash nano .env

  3. Ensure the file contains exactly the following values. Copy and paste these lines into the file:

    ```env SUPABASE_URL=your_supabase_url SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_supabase_anon_key MISTRAL_API_KEY=your_mistral_api_key

    STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=your_stripe_secret_key STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=your_stripe_publishable_key STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_stripe_webhook_secret

docs.text: CELERY_BROKER_URL=redis://redis:6379/0 CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND=redis://redis:6379/0 `` 4. Save the file and exit the editor (Ctrl+O,Enter,Ctrl+X`).

docs.text:
You need to create the necessary tables in your Supabase database.

  1. Go to your Supabase Dashboard.
  2. Navigate to the SQL Editor.
  3. Create a new query and paste the contents of the following files (found in the backend/sql/ directory):
    • create_subscriptions_table.sql
    • create_historical_extractions_table.sql
    • create_user_sessions_table.sql
  4. Run the queries to create the tables.

docs.title: Step 5: Stripe Setup
docs.text:
Before running the application, you must configure your Stripe account.

  1. Follow the instructions in STRIPE_SETUP.md to:
    • Get your API Keys.
    • Create your Products and get Price IDs.
    • Set up the Stripe CLI for local webhooks.
  2. Update your .env file with the Price IDs and API Keys obtained from Stripe.

docs.title: Step 6: Configure Nginx for Localhost
docs.text:
The default Nginx configuration is set up for production (SSL, domain name). For local development, we need a simpler configuration.

  1. Create/Overwrite the nginx/nginx.conf file: bash nano nginx/nginx.conf

  2. Delete any existing content and paste the following Localhost Configuration:

    ```nginx upstream backend { server backend:8000; }

    upstream frontend { server frontend:80; }

    server { listen 80; server_name localhost; client_max_body_size 50M;

    # Frontend
location / {
    proxy_pass http://frontend;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

# Backend API
location /api {
    rewrite ^/api(.*)$ $1 break;
    proxy_pass http://backend;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}

# Health check
location /health {
    proxy_pass http://backend/;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
}

    } `` 3. Save and exit (Ctrl+O,Enter,Ctrl+X`).

docs.text:
1. In the same terminal (inside the nolain-ocr directory), run the following command to build and start all services: bash docker-compose up -d --build This process may take a few minutes the first time as it downloads images and builds the application.

  2. Check if all containers are running: bash docker-compose ps You should see nolain-ocr-backend, nolain-ocr-frontend, nolain-ocr-celery-worker, nolain-ocr-redis, and nolain-ocr-nginx all listed with status "Up".

docs.title: Step 6: SSL Certificate Setup (First Time Only)
docs.text:
We need to obtain SSL certificates from Let's Encrypt.

  1. Create the necessary directories for Certbot: bash mkdir -p certbot/conf certbot/www

  2. Create a temporary Nginx configuration file: bash nano nginx/nginx-temp.conf

  3. Paste the following content into nginx/nginx-temp.conf: nginx upstream backend { server backend:8000; } upstream frontend { server frontend:80; } server { listen 80; server_name nolainocr.com www.nolainocr.com; location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ { root /var/www/certbot; } location / { return 200 'OK'; add_header Content-Type text/plain; } } (Replace nolainocr.com with your actual domain if different)

  4. Swap the configuration and start Nginx: bash # Backup current config (likely the localhost one) cp nginx/nginx.conf nginx/nginx.conf.backup # Use temporary config for SSL challenge cp nginx/nginx-temp.conf nginx/nginx.conf docker-compose up -d nginx

  5. Run Certbot to get the certificates (Replace YOUR_EMAIL and DOMAIN): bash docker run -it --rm \ -v "$(pwd)/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt" \ -v "$(pwd)/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot" \ certbot/certbot certonly \ --webroot \ --webroot-path=/var/www/certbot \ --email YOUR_EMAIL@example.com \ --agree-tos \ --no-eff-email \ -d nolainocr.com \ -d www.nolainocr.com

  6. Use the Production Nginx configuration: bash # Use the production config which includes SSL and domain settings cp nginx/nginx-production.conf nginx/nginx.conf rm nginx/nginx-temp.conf

docs.title: Step 7: Run the Application
docs.text:
1. Stop the temporary Nginx container: bash docker-compose down
  2. Build and start the full application in production mode: bash docker-compose up -d --build

docs.title: Step 8: Setup Auto-Renewal
docs.text:
SSL certificates expire every 90 days. Set up a cron job to renew them automatically.

  1. Open the crontab editor: bash crontab -e
  2. Add the following line at the bottom (replace /path/to/nolain-ocr with the actual path, e.g., /root/nolain-ocr): 0 0,12 * * * cd /path/to/nolain-ocr && docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt" -v "$(pwd)/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot" certbot/certbot renew && docker-compose restart nginx >> /var/log/ssl-renewal.log 2>&1

docs.title: Password Reset Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to configure Supabase for the complete password reset flow.

docs.title: Supabase Configuration
docs.text: To enable the password reset functionality, you need to configure the redirect URL in your Supabase project:

docs.title: 1. Access Supabase Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Go to Supabase Dashboard
  2. Select your project
  3. Navigate to Authentication → URL Configuration

docs.title: 2. Configure Redirect URLs
docs.text:
IMPORTANT: This is the crucial step that determines where users are redirected when they click the reset link in their email.

In the Redirect URLs section, add the following URL:

http://localhost:3000/reset-password

For production, replace localhost:3000 with your actual domain:

https://yourdomain.com/reset-password

Note: Make sure this URL exactly matches your frontend route /reset-password. This is where users will be taken when they click the "Reset password" button in the email.

docs.title: 3. Configure Site URL
docs.text:
Make sure your Site URL is set to your frontend URL:

  • Development: http://localhost:3000
  • Production: https://yourdomain.com

docs.title: 4. Backend Environment Variable (Optional)
docs.text:
For production deployments, you can set the FRONTEND_URL environment variable in your backend to ensure the correct redirect URL is used:

# In your .env file or environment variables
FRONTEND_URL=https://yourdomain.com

If not set, it defaults to http://localhost:3000 for development.

docs.title: 5. Email Templates (Optional)
docs.text:
You can customize the password reset email template:

  1. Go to Authentication → Email Templates
  2. Select Reset Password
  3. Customize the template as needed
  4. The reset link will automatically redirect to /reset-password with the required tokens

Important: The email template will contain a "Reset password" button/link. When users click this link, they will be redirected to the URL you configured in step 2 above (/reset-password).

docs.title: How the Flow Works
docs.text:
1. User requests password reset: Clicks "Forgot password?" on login form
  2. Email sent: Supabase sends password reset email with secure link
  3. User clicks link: Redirected to /reset-password with access_token and refresh_token
  4. Password update: User enters new password, which is updated via Supabase API
  5. Success: User is redirected to login page with success message

docs.title: Visual Flow Diagram
docs.text:
User clicks "Forgot password?" 
         ↓
   /forgot-password page
         ↓
   User enters email
         ↓
   Supabase sends email
         ↓
   User clicks "Reset password" in email
         ↓
   Redirected to /reset-password (with tokens)
         ↓
   User enters new password
         ↓
   Password updated successfully
         ↓
   Redirected to /login

Key Point: The redirect from the email to /reset-password is controlled by the Redirect URLs setting in Supabase. Make sure this is configured correctly!

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• The reset tokens are only valid for a limited time (configurable in Supabase)
  • Tokens are single-use and expire after password update
  • The /reset-password page validates tokens before allowing password update
  • All password updates are handled securely through Supabase's authentication system

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
To test the password reset flow:

  1. Start your frontend and backend servers
  2. Go to the login page
  3. Click "Forgot password?"
  4. Enter a valid email address
  5. Check your email for the reset link
  6. Click the link to test the password update flow

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
1. "Invalid password reset link" error: Check that the redirect URL is correctly configured in Supabase
  2. User redirected to landing page instead of reset page:
  3. Verify the Redirect URL in Supabase is set to http://localhost:3000/reset-password (or your production domain)
  4. Make sure the URL exactly matches your frontend route
  5. Check that there are no typos in the redirect URL
  6. IMPORTANT: The backend now explicitly sets the redirect URL when sending the email. Check the backend logs to see what redirect URL is being used

  7. Ensure your frontend is running on the correct port (3000 by default)

  8. "otp_expired" or "access_denied" error in URL:

  9. This means the password reset link has expired (usually expires in 1 hour)
  10. The page now handles this error gracefully and shows a "Request New Password Reset" button
  11. Try requesting a new password reset immediately after the error
  12. Check if your system clock is correct (timezone issues can cause early expiration)
  13. "Password update failed" error: Ensure the tokens are valid and not expired
  14. Email not received: Check spam folder and verify email configuration in Supabase
  15. Tokens not found in URL: Check that the redirect URL includes the tokens as query parameters

docs.title: Debug Steps
docs.text:
1. Check browser console: Open browser dev tools and look for console logs when the password reset page loads
  2. Check backend logs: Look for the redirect URL being used when sending the email
  3. Verify Supabase configuration: Ensure Redirect URLs match your frontend URL
  4. Test the URL directly: Try accessing http://localhost:3000/reset-password?access_token=test&refresh_token=test to see if the page loads
  5. Check environment variables: Ensure FRONTEND_URL is set correctly in your backend

pages = round(top_up_amount_usd ÷ price_per_page_usd)

STRIPE_API_TOPUP_10_PRICE_ID=price_...

docs.title: Table 1: user_sessions
docs.text:
Purpose: Track active upload sessions

Go to SQL Editor and run:

CREATE TABLE user_sessions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL,
    folder_path TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Index for faster lookups
CREATE INDEX idx_user_sessions_user_id ON user_sessions(user_id);

docs.title: Table 2: historical_extractions
docs.text:
Purpose: Store extraction results

CREATE TABLE historical_extractions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL,
    historical_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    data_content JSONB NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_historical_user_id ON historical_extractions(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_historical_name ON historical_extractions(user_id, historical_name);

-- Update timestamp trigger
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at = NOW();
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

CREATE TRIGGER update_historical_extractions_updated_at
    BEFORE UPDATE ON historical_extractions
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

docs.title: Table 3: subscriptions
docs.text:
Purpose: Track user subscriptions and usage

CREATE TABLE subscriptions (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    user_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    plan_tier TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'free',
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    total_pages_processed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    stripe_customer_id TEXT,
    stripe_subscription_id TEXT,
    current_period_start TIMESTAMPTZ,
    current_period_end TIMESTAMPTZ,
    cancel_at_period_end BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Index
CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_user_id ON subscriptions(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_stripe_customer ON subscriptions(stripe_customer_id);

-- Update timestamp trigger
CREATE TRIGGER update_subscriptions_updated_at
    BEFORE UPDATE ON subscriptions
    FOR EACH ROW
    EXECUTE FUNCTION update_updated_at_column();

docs.title: Docker Setup Guide
docs.text: This document explains the process of dockerizing and running the Nolain OCR application using Docker and Docker Compose.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The application is containerized using Docker and orchestrated with Docker Compose. It consists of three main services:

  1. Backend: FastAPI application running on Python 3.11
  2. Frontend: React/TypeScript application built with Vite and served via Nginx
  3. Nginx: Reverse proxy handling routing and SSL termination

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────┐
│   Nginx (443)   │ ← External access
└────────┬────────┘
         │
    ┌────┴────┐
    │         │
┌───▼───┐ ┌──▼──────┐
│Frontend│ │ Backend │
│  :80  │ │  :8000  │
└───────┘ └─────────┘
  • Nginx listens on ports 80 (HTTP) and 443 (HTTPS)
  • Frontend serves static files on port 80 (internal)
  • Backend API runs on port 8000 (internal)
  • All services communicate through a Docker bridge network

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have the following installed:

  • Docker (version 20.10 or higher)
  • Docker Compose (version 1.29 or higher)
  • Git (to clone the repository)

Verify your installation:

docker --version
docker-compose --version

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root with the following variables:

# Supabase Configuration
SUPABASE_URL=your_supabase_url
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your_supabase_anon_key

# Mistral AI Configuration
MISTRAL_API_KEY=your_mistral_api_key

# Stripe Configuration
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=your_stripe_secret_key
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_stripe_webhook_secret

# Frontend URL (for CORS and redirects)
FRONTEND_URL=https://nolainocr.com

Note: For local development, you may want to set FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost or adjust the nginx configuration accordingly.

docs.title: Option 1: Build All Services with Docker Compose
docs.text:
Build all services at once:

docker-compose build

Build without cache (useful for fresh builds):

docker-compose build --no-cache

docs.title: Option 2: Build Individual Services
docs.text:
Build only the backend:

docker-compose build backend

Build only the frontend:

docker-compose build frontend

docs.title: Backend Dockerfile
docs.text:
The backend uses a multi-stage approach:

  1. Base Image: python:3.11-slim
  2. System Dependencies: Installs poppler-utils for PDF processing
  3. Python Dependencies: Installs packages from requirements.txt
  4. Application Code: Copies the backend directory
  5. Runtime: Runs with uvicorn on port 8000

Key features: - Optimized layer caching (requirements copied first) - Data directory created for file uploads - Exposes port 8000 internally

docs.title: Frontend Dockerfile
docs.text:
The frontend uses a multi-stage build:

  1. Builder Stage:
  2. Uses node:18-alpine as base
  3. Installs dependencies with npm ci

  4. Builds the production bundle with npm run build

  5. Production Stage:

  6. Uses nginx:alpine for serving static files
  7. Copies built files from builder stage
  8. Includes nginx configuration for SPA routing

Key features: - Multi-stage build reduces final image size - Production-optimized build - Nginx configured for React Router (SPA routing)

docs.title: Start All Services
docs.text:
Start all services in detached mode:

docker-compose up -d

Start with logs visible:

docker-compose up

docs.title: Stop Services
docs.text:
Stop all services:

docker-compose down

Stop and remove volumes (⚠️ removes data):

docker-compose down -v

docs.title: View Logs
docs.text:
View logs from all services:

docker-compose logs -f

View logs from a specific service:

docker-compose logs -f backend
docker-compose logs -f frontend
docker-compose logs -f nginx

docs.title: Restart Services
docs.text:
Restart all services:

docker-compose restart

Restart a specific service:

docker-compose restart backend

docs.title: Backend Service
docs.text:
• Container Name: nolain-ocr-backend
  • Internal Port: 8000
  • Working Directory: /app
  • Volumes:
  • ./backend/data:/app/backend/data (persistent data storage)
  • Environment Variables: All variables from .env file
  • Restart Policy: unless-stopped

Access the backend API: - Internally: http://backend:8000 - Externally: https://your-domain.com/api

docs.title: Frontend Service
docs.text:
• Container Name: nolain-ocr-frontend
  • Internal Port: 80
  • Restart Policy: unless-stopped

Access the frontend: - Internally: http://frontend:80 - Externally: https://your-domain.com

docs.title: Nginx Service
docs.text:
• Container Name: nolain-ocr-nginx
  • External Ports: 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS)
  • Volumes:
  • ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro (nginx config)
  • ./certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt:ro (SSL certificates)
  • ./certbot/www:/var/www/certbot:ro (Let's Encrypt challenges)
  • Depends On: backend, frontend
  • Restart Policy: unless-stopped

Nginx handles: - SSL/TLS termination - HTTP to HTTPS redirects - Reverse proxying to backend (/api routes) - Serving frontend static files - Let's Encrypt certificate challenges

docs.title: Check Service Status
docs.text: docker-compose ps

docs.title: Inspect a Container
docs.text:
docker inspect nolain-ocr-backend
docker inspect nolain-ocr-frontend
docker inspect nolain-ocr-nginx

docs.title: Execute Commands in Containers
docs.text:
Access backend container shell:

docker-compose exec backend bash

Access frontend container shell:

docker-compose exec frontend sh

docs.title: Port Already in Use
docs.text:
If ports 80 or 443 are already in use:

# Find process using port 80
sudo lsof -i :80

# Find process using port 443
sudo lsof -i :443

Stop the conflicting service or modify docker-compose.yml to use different ports.

docs.title: Environment Variables Not Loading
docs.text:
Ensure your .env file is in the project root and contains all required variables:

# Verify .env file exists
ls -la .env

# Check if variables are loaded
docker-compose config

docs.title: Build Failures
docs.text:
Clear Docker cache and rebuild:

docker-compose down
docker system prune -a
docker-compose build --no-cache

docs.title: Frontend Not Updating
docs.text:
Rebuild the frontend after code changes:

docker-compose build frontend
docker-compose up -d frontend

docs.text:
Check if backend is running:

docker-compose logs backend

docs.title: Nginx Configuration Errors

Test nginx configuration:

docker-compose exec nginx nginx -t

Reload nginx after config changes:

docker-compose exec nginx nginx -s reload

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
Check if services are responding:

# Backend health
curl http://localhost/api/health

# Frontend
curl http://localhost

docs.title: View Resource Usage
docs.text: docker stats

docs.title: Clean Up
docs.text:
Remove all containers, networks, and images:

docker-compose down --rmi all

Remove unused Docker resources:

docker system prune -a --volumes

docs.title: Making Changes
docs.text:
1. Backend Changes: bash # After modifying backend code docker-compose build backend docker-compose up -d backend

  2. Frontend Changes: bash # After modifying frontend code docker-compose build frontend docker-compose up -d frontend

  3. Nginx Configuration Changes: bash # After modifying nginx.conf docker-compose restart nginx # Or reload without restart docker-compose exec nginx nginx -s reload

docs.title: Hot Reloading (Development)
docs.text: For development with hot reloading, you may want to run services locally instead of in Docker, or mount volumes for live code updates (requires additional docker-compose configuration).

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
1. SSL Certificates: Ensure Let's Encrypt certificates are properly configured
  2. Environment Variables: Use secure secret management in production
  3. Data Persistence: Backend data directory is mounted as a volume
  4. Logging: Consider setting up centralized logging
  5. Monitoring: Add health checks and monitoring tools
  6. Backup: Implement regular backups of the data directory
  7. Resource Limits: Consider adding resource limits in docker-compose.yml:
services:
  backend:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2'
          memory: 2G

docs.title: Domain and SSL Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide will help you: 1. Link your domain (nolainocr.com) to your VPS IP 2. Set up HTTPS/SSL certificates for secure connections

docs.title: ✅ What Has Been Configured in the Codebase
docs.text:
The following changes have been made to your repository:

  1. Nginx Configuration (nginx/nginx.conf):
  2. Added HTTPS server block listening on port 443
  3. Configured SSL certificate paths
  4. Added HTTP to HTTPS redirect
  5. Added security headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)

  6. Configured for both nolainocr.com and www.nolainocr.com

  7. Docker Compose (docker-compose.yml):

  8. Added port 443 mapping for HTTPS
  9. Added volumes for SSL certificates (certbot/conf and certbot/www)

  10. Updated FRONTEND_URL to use HTTPS

  11. Backend CORS (backend/main.py):

  12. Updated CORS to allow your production domains
  13. Allows: https://nolainocr.com, https://www.nolainocr.com, and http://localhost (for development)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Domain: nolainocr.com (purchased from Hostinger)
  • VPS IP address from Contabo
  • SSH access to your VPS
  • Docker and Docker Compose installed on the VPS

docs.title: Step 1: Configure DNS in Hostinger
docs.text:
1. Log in to your Hostinger account
  2. Go to Domains → Select nolainocr.com
  3. Navigate to DNS / Name Servers section
  4. Add the following DNS records:

docs.title: A Record (Main Domain)
docs.text:
• Type: A
  • Name: @ (or leave blank)
  • Value: [Your VPS IP Address]
  • TTL: 3600 (or default)

docs.title: A Record (WWW Subdomain)
docs.text:
• Type: A
  • Name: www
  • Value: [Your VPS IP Address]
  • TTL: 3600 (or default)

docs.title: Optional: CNAME Record (Alternative)
docs.text:
If Hostinger doesn't support A record for www, you can use: - Type: CNAME - Name: www - Value: nolainocr.com - TTL: 3600

  1. Save the DNS records

Note: DNS propagation can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours, but typically takes 1-2 hours. You can check if DNS has propagated using:

dig nolainocr.com
# or
nslookup nolainocr.com

docs.title: Step 2: Initial Nginx Setup (Before SSL)
docs.text:
Before obtaining SSL certificates, we need to temporarily allow HTTP access for Let's Encrypt validation.

  1. On your VPS, create the certbot directories:
mkdir -p certbot/conf certbot/www
  1. Make sure your docker-compose is running and nginx is accessible on port 80:
docker-compose up -d
  1. Verify nginx is running:
docker ps | grep nginx

docs.title: Step 3: Obtain SSL Certificates
docs.text: We'll use Certbot to obtain Let's Encrypt SSL certificates. The easiest method is using Certbot with Docker.

docs.title: Method 1: Using Certbot Docker Container (Recommended)
docs.text:
On your VPS, follow these steps:

  1. Create certbot directories:
cd /path/to/your/project
mkdir -p certbot/conf certbot/www
  1. Create a temporary nginx config for certbot validation:
  2. Create a file nginx/nginx-temp.conf with this content:
upstream backend {
    server backend:8000;
}

upstream frontend {
    server frontend:80;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name nolainocr.com www.nolainocr.com;

    location /.well-known/acme-challenge/ {
        root /var/www/certbot;
    }

    location / {
        return 200 'OK';
        add_header Content-Type text/plain;
    }
}
  1. Backup and temporarily replace nginx config:
cp nginx/nginx.conf nginx/nginx.conf.backup
cp nginx/nginx-temp.conf nginx/nginx.conf
  1. Restart nginx with temporary config:
docker-compose up -d nginx
  1. Run Certbot to obtain certificates:
docker run -it --rm \
  -v "$(pwd)/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt" \
  -v "$(pwd)/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot" \
  certbot/certbot certonly \
  --webroot \
  --webroot-path=/var/www/certbot \
  --email YOUR_EMAIL@example.com \
  --agree-tos \
  --no-eff-email \
  -d nolainocr.com \
  -d www.nolainocr.com

Replace YOUR_EMAIL@example.com with your actual email address.

  1. Restore the original nginx config:
cp nginx/nginx.conf.backup nginx/nginx.conf
docker-compose up -d nginx
  1. Clean up temporary file:
rm nginx/nginx-temp.conf

docs.title: Method 2: Using Certbot Installed on Host
docs.text:
If you prefer to install Certbot directly on your VPS:

  1. Install Certbot:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install certbot -y
  1. Stop nginx container:
docker-compose stop nginx
  1. Run Certbot in standalone mode:
sudo certbot certonly --standalone \
  -d nolainocr.com \
  -d www.nolainocr.com \
  --email YOUR_EMAIL@example.com \
  --agree-tos \
  --no-eff-email
  1. Copy certificates to the certbot directory:
cd /path/to/your/project
mkdir -p certbot/conf/live certbot/conf/archive
sudo cp -r /etc/letsencrypt/live/nolainocr.com certbot/conf/live/
sudo cp -r /etc/letsencrypt/archive/nolainocr.com certbot/conf/archive/
sudo chown -R $USER:$USER certbot/
  1. Start nginx:
docker-compose up -d nginx

docs.title: Step 4: Verify SSL Setup
docs.text:
1. Restart your services:
docker-compose restart
  1. Check if certificates are mounted correctly:
docker exec nolain-ocr-nginx ls -la /etc/letsencrypt/live/nolainocr.com/
  1. Check nginx is running:
docker ps | grep nginx
  1. Test your website:
  2. Visit https://nolainocr.com in your browser
  3. You should see a padlock icon (🔒) indicating the site is secure
  4. HTTP should automatically redirect to HTTPS
  5. Test https://www.nolainocr.com as well

docs.title: Step 5: Set Up Auto-Renewal
docs.text:
SSL certificates expire every 90 days. Set up automatic renewal using cron:

On your VPS:

  1. Open crontab for editing:
crontab -e
  1. Add this line (replace /path/to/your/project with your actual project path):
0 0,12 * * * cd /path/to/your/project && docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/certbot/conf:/etc/letsencrypt" -v "$(pwd)/certbot/www:/var/www/certbot" certbot/certbot renew && docker-compose restart nginx >> /var/log/ssl-renewal.log 2>&1

This will check for certificate renewal twice daily (at midnight and noon) and restart nginx if certificates are renewed.

docs.title: Step 6: Firewall Configuration (If Needed)
docs.text:
If your VPS firewall is enabled, ensure ports 80 and 443 are open:

sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw status

docs.title: DNS Not Propagating
docs.text:
• Wait 1-2 hours for DNS propagation
  • Check DNS propagation: https://www.whatsmydns.net/
  • Clear your local DNS cache: sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches (Linux)

docs.title: SSL Certificate Issues
docs.text:

  • Check nginx logs: docker logs nolain-ocr-nginx
  • Ensure port 443 is open in your VPS firewall
  • Verify domain points to correct IP: dig nolainocr.com

docs.title: Port 80/443 Not Accessible
docs.text:
• Check firewall rules: bash sudo ufw status sudo ufw allow 80/tcp sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
  • Check if ports are in use: sudo netstat -tulpn | grep -E ':(80|443)'

docs.title: Nginx Container Issues
docs.text:
• Check container status: docker ps -a
  • View logs: docker logs nolain-ocr-nginx
  • Restart container: docker-compose restart nginx

docs.title: Security Checklist
docs.text:
• ✅ HTTPS enabled and working
  • ✅ HTTP redirects to HTTPS
  • ✅ SSL certificates obtained and mounted
  • ✅ Auto-renewal configured
  • ✅ Security headers added (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
  • ✅ Firewall configured (ports 80, 443 open)
